newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke - no need for tax rise to cut PSBR.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke - no need for tax rise to cut PSBR.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Tuesday he saw no need for tax rises after approaching elections to cut Britain's public sector deficit.
Clarke had been asked whether tax increases were inevitable whoever wins the coming election. "No, definitely not," he replied. "It's become a popular theory which I entirely reject."

Clarke said it was impossible to prove that Britain's budget deficit should be smaller than it is at the present stage of the economic cycle and expressed confidence that a combination of sustained growth and tight control of public spending would enable the government to meet its goal of eliminating the budget deficit in the medium-term.
Elections must be held by May, with Prime Minister John Major believed to favour May 1.
